title: Deep house
description: Piano stabs, organ bass and a shuffled groove: the warm side of 90s house, on the skills from the core lessons.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Deep house basics
tracks.blurb: A piano stab, an organ bass, a shuffle, a groove, then a hook and an 8-bar phrase.

lessons.title: The piano stab
lessons.goal: Add a sampled piano chord on the offbeats of 2 and 4.
lessons.concept:
Deep house grew out of Chicago house and New York garage, and its signature sound is a **sampled piano** playing short minor-seventh chords. The chord lands on the **offbeats** of beats 2 and 4, so it answers the clap rather than sitting on it.

`chord("Cm7").voicing()` picks the notes; `.struct("[~ x]*2")` says when they hit: a rest, then a hit, twice a bar. `s("piano")` is a sampled grand piano.

A little **reverb** (`.room`) pushes the piano back behind the drums, which is where deep house keeps it.

tasks.text: Add a part called piano: a Cm7 chord on the piano sound, hitting on the offbeats of beats 2 and 4.
tasks.hint: const piano = chord("Cm7").voicing().struct("[~ x]*2").s("piano").gain(.6), then add piano to the stack.

tasks.text: Push the piano back with a little reverb.

challenge.text: Make the chord change every bar: Cm7, then Fm7.
challenge.hint: chord("<Cm7 Fm7>"): angle brackets pick one chord per bar.

summary: The deep house piano is a minor 7th chord on the offbeats of 2 and 4.
chord(…).voicing().struct("[~ x]*2") picks the notes and when they hit.
A touch of .room() puts it behind the drums.

lessons.title: The organ bass
lessons.goal: Write a short, hollow bassline that bounces against the kick.
lessons.concept:
The classic deep house bass is an **organ bass**: a hollow, woody tone (a **square** wave) played in short stabs between the kicks, often with a pure **sine** underneath to carry the weight.

A square wave through a low-pass filter already sounds like a cheap organ. Keep the notes short with a fast **decay** and no **sustain**, and put them on the **offbeats** so they never fight the kick.

We stay in C minor, like the piano, so the notes agree: `n("0 … 3").scale("C2:minor")` picks scale degrees, and the 2 in the scale name puts them in the second octave.

tasks.text: Add a part called bass: a square wave playing scale degrees of C minor, down in octave 2, on every offbeat.
tasks.hint: const bass = n("[~ 0] [~ 0] [~ 3] [~ 0]").scale("C2:minor").s("square"), and stack it.

tasks.text: Make every bass note a short stab: a quick decay and no sustain.
Round it off with a low-pass filter around 700 Hz.

challenge.text: Add a sine sub an octave below the bass, on the same notes.
challenge.hint: const sub = n("[~ 0] [~ 0] [~ 3] [~ 0]").scale("C1:minor").s("sine").decay(.2).sustain(0).gain(.7), and stack it.

summary: An organ bass is a square wave played in short offbeat stabs.
Short decay, no sustain and a low-pass around 700 Hz make it hollow and woody.
scale("C2:minor"): the number picks the octave.
A sine an octave below carries the weight.

lessons.title: Shuffle and ghosts
lessons.goal: Give the hats a deep house shuffle and add ghost notes.
lessons.concept:
Deep house moves because the hats **shuffle**: every second 16th arrives a touch late. On an MPC you'd set swing to 56–58%; here `.swingBy(.14, 8)` does the same (x = (swing% − 50) / 50).

**Ghost notes** are hits so quiet you feel them more than hear them: a rimshot or a quiet snare between the main hits. They fill the gaps without crowding the groove.

tasks.text: Make the closed hats play 16ths, with the hit on each beat louder than the ones between.
Shuffle them: a swing of about 57%.

challenge.text: Add ghost rimshots: a part called ghosts with two quiet rim hits per bar, off the beat.
challenge.hint: const ghosts = s("[~ ~ ~ rim] [~ ~ rim ~]").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.25), and stack it.

summary: Swing delays every second 16th; .swingBy(.14, 8) is about 57%.
A gain pattern on 16th hats puts the weight on the beat.
Ghost notes are quiet in-between hits that fill the groove.

lessons.title: Project: Deep house groove
lessons.goal: Put the piano, the organ bass and the shuffle together in one groove.
lessons.concept:
Everything from this pack in one loop: a shuffled 909 groove, the organ bass in the gaps, and the piano answering the clap. Keep it **deep**: nothing loud, the piano behind the drums, the bass felt more than heard.

The tempo sits a little slower than the core lessons, 118–122 BPM. One `const key` keeps the bass and the piano in tune, so changing the key later is one edit.

tasks.text: Add shuffled 16th hats (gain pattern, swing about 57%) and stack them.
Add the organ bass in the key, on the offbeats, short and filtered.
Add the piano stab, two chords alternating, behind the drums.

challenge.text: Double the clap on the last bar of every four.
challenge.hint: Add .lastOf(4, x => x.ply(2)) to the clap line.

summary: A deep house groove: shuffled hats, an offbeat organ bass, a piano stab behind the drums.
One const key keeps the bass and piano in tune.
A fill every four bars (.lastOf) marks the phrase.

lessons.title: The organ riff
lessons.goal: Write a hook: a one-bar organ riff in the key, in 8ths.
lessons.concept:
Deep house hooks are often not sung. A short **organ riff**, two or three notes in 8th notes with rests between, repeats until it becomes the song.

The riff lives an octave above the bass, in the same key: `n("0 ~ 3 ~ 4 ~ 3 ~").scale("C3:minor")`. The 3 in the scale name puts it in the third octave. Keep it short and dry, then give it a little room so it sits with the piano.

tasks.text: Add a part called riff: a square organ playing degrees 0, 3 and 4 of C minor in 8ths with rests, octave 3, short.
tasks.hint: const riff = n("0 ~ 3 ~ 4 ~ 3 ~").scale("C3:minor").s("square").decay(.15).sustain(0).lpf(1200).gain(.4), and stack it.

tasks.text: Give the riff its own small room, on its own orbit.

challenge.text: Answer the riff every other bar with a different ending.

summary: A hook can be three notes in 8ths with rests.
< > gives the riff a question and an answer.

lessons.title: The 8-bar phrase
lessons.goal: Make the loop change every eight bars.
lessons.concept:
House is counted in **eights**. A loop that never changes feels like a demo; one that marks every eighth bar feels like a record. The marks are small: a doubled clap in bar 8, open hats that arrive for the second half of the phrase, a kick that drops out for one bar before the next eight.

`.lastOf(8, f)` applies a change in the last bar of every eight. `.mask("<0 0 0 0 1 1 1 1>")` silences a part for the first four bars of each eight and lets it through for the rest.

tasks.text: Double the clap in the last bar of every eight.
tasks.hint: .lastOf(8, x => x.ply(2)) on the clap line.

tasks.text: Add open hats on the offbeats that only play in bars 5 to 8 of each eight.
tasks.hint: const open = s("[~ oh]*4").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.4).mask("<0 0 0 0 1 1 1 1>"), and stack it.

challenge.text: Drop the kick for the last bar of every eight.

summary: .lastOf(8, f) marks the last bar of each eight.
.mask("<0 0 0 0 1 1 1 1>") lets a part in for half the phrase.
